ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Power, CardRarity.Rare, TargetType.Self)` (CrimsonMantle.cs:19-22) == cost 1 / POWER / RARE / SELF. No keywords. It does NOT override GainsBlock even though the power grants block, so the sim's `gains_block` default of False is right and Nimble's CanEnchant refuses it on both sides.

OnPlay.rationale: `PowerCmd.Apply<CrimsonMantlePower>(..., DynamicVars["CrimsonMantlePower"].BaseValue, ...)` followed by `?.IncrementSelfDamage()` on the RETURNED power (CrimsonMantle.cs:28) == `PowerCmd.apply(...)` then `ctx.player.powers.get('crimson_mantle')` and `power.increment_self_damage()` (crimson_mantle.py:37-42). The sim has no return value from `PowerCmd.apply`, so it re-fetches the power by id; on the normal path both reach the same instance and increment it exactly once per play. Presentation, folded in: NPowerUpVfx (26) and TriggerAnim (27).

guards.what: C# skips IncrementSelfDamage when Apply returns NULL; check whether the sim still increments whenever the power is present (CrimsonMantle.cs:28 vs crimson_mantle.py:40-42)
guards.rationale: REVISED 2026-08-04 (stale-sweep re-audit; `sts2_rl/cmds.py` changed since the 2026-07-26 audit). At that time `PowerCmd.apply` returned nothing and every card re-fetched the power by id, so `on_play` could not tell a null Apply from a successful one and always incremented -- that was a real gap. `PowerCmd.apply` now RETURNS the applied/stacked instance or `None` (`sts2_rl/cmds.py:851-859`, docstring 866-881), explicitly mirroring `Apply<T>`'s return contract (PowerCmd.cs:60-88): `None` on `is_ending` (cmds.py:890-891, <-> IsEnding, PowerCmd.cs:69-72), on `not can_receive_powers` (cmds.py:901-902, <-> !CanReceivePowers, PowerCmd.cs:73-76), and on the stacking `ModifyAmount` chain resolving to 0 (cmds.py's `existing is not None` branch below :937, <-> PowerCmd.cs:84-87). `crimson_mantle.py:37-42` now does `power = PowerCmd.apply(...)` then `if power is not None: power.increment_self_damage()`, which is exactly the C# null-conditional `?.IncrementSelfDamage()` (CrimsonMantle.cs:28). The one documented narrowing left in `PowerCmd.apply` -- C# additionally returns a non-null but UNATTACHED PowerModel when a brand-new instance's raw amount is 0 (Apply<T> line 79-83 sets `power` before the inner `Apply`'s own `amount==0` early-return at PowerCmd.cs:103, so it is never nulled back out), while the sim returns `None` for that same `existing is None and amount == 0` case (cmds.py:937-938) -- does not apply here: Crimson Mantle's own play never calls `PowerCmd.apply` with a raw amount of 0 (its `_power_amount` is a fixed 8/10, never itself modified before the call), so that branch is unreached by this card. That narrowing is the pre-existing, separately-filed dormant gap `card/the_bomb/g1`; per binding rule 3 (one mechanism, one verdict) it is not re-filed here.
